ServiceDescriptor.description: A legacy service descriptor, the way otoroshi 17 and older described a service. Its main fields are described here, the other ones (headers, security, client settings, canary, plugins, ...) are read the way otoroshi 17 wrote them. Every field is optional: the template of a new descriptor gives the missing ones

id.description: The id of the descriptor, kept as the id of the route

name.description: The name of the descriptor, given to the converted route

description.description: The description of the descriptor, given to the converted route

groups.description: The ids of the service groups of the descriptor

items.description: The id of a service group

env.description: The environment of the descriptor, part of its legacy domain (`<subdomain>.<env>.<domain>`, without the env when it is `prod`)

domain.description: The domain of the legacy domain of the descriptor

subdomain.description: The subdomain of the legacy domain of the descriptor

hosts.description: The hosts the descriptor matches, besides the legacy domain built from `subdomain`, `env` and `domain` (unless `handleLegacyDomain` is false). Each host, followed by each of the `paths` (by `matchingRoot`, or `/`, when there is none), becomes a domain of the converted route

paths.description: The path prefixes the descriptor matches on each of its hosts. Each of them, after each host, becomes a domain of the converted route

matchingRoot.description: The path prefix the descriptor matches, removed from the forwarded path

stripPath.description: Whether the matched path is removed from the forwarded path

root.description: The path prefix of the calls forwarded to the targets

targets.description: The targets the calls are forwarded to

items.description: A target of the descriptor. Its other fields (protocol, predicate, ip address, mtls configuration, backup, ...) are read the way otoroshi 17 wrote them

host.description: The host of the target, with its port if any

scheme.description: The scheme of the target, `https` by default

weight.description: The weight of the target in the load balancing, 1 by default

publicPatterns.description: The regular expressions of the paths that need no api key

privatePatterns.description: The regular expressions of the paths that need an api key even when they match a public pattern

forceHttps.description: Whether http calls are redirected to https

metadata.description: Free key/value pairs attached to the descriptor, given to the converted route along with the `otoroshi-core-` keys that keep its legacy settings (`otoroshi-core-legacy`, `otoroshi-core-env`...)

tags.description: Free tags of the descriptor, given to the converted route with an `env:<env>` tag added

TryItCookie.description: A cookie of a trial: one the request sends, or one the response sets

max_age.description: The lifetime of the cookie, in seconds

secure.description: Whether the cookie is only sent over https. Defaults to `false`

http_only.description: Whether the cookie is hidden from the scripts of the page. Defaults to `false`

sameSite.description: The same site policy of a cookie the response sets, when it has one

TryItRequest.description: The request of a trial, sent through the route by the node answering the admin api, from `127.0.0.1`. Every field is optional: an empty body is a `GET` on the path of the first domain of the route

method.description: The http method of the request. Defaults to `GET`

path.description: The path of the request, with its query string, starting with `/`. Defaults to the path of the first domain of the route: for a route of an api, the context path of the api followed by the path of the route

headers.description: The headers of the request. `Host` is the first domain of the route, whatever the headers say

body.description: The body of the request, as text, or encoded in base64 when `base_64` is `true`. No body when absent or empty

base_64.description: Whether `body` is encoded in base64, for a binary body. Defaults to `false`

client_cert.description: The id of a certificate of the store that the request presents as its client certificate, for a route that checks the client certificate (mtls). The admin behind the credentials has to be able to read it

ExecutionReportStep.description: A step of the engine in the handling of a call

task.description: The name of the step, in the order the engine runs them: `start-handling`, `check-concurrent-requests`, `find-route`, `compute-plugins`, `check-global-maintenance`, `call-before-request-callbacks`, `extract-tracking-id`, `call-pre-route-plugins`, `call-access-validator-plugins`, `update-apikey-quotas`, `choose-backend`, `transform-request`, `call-backend`, `transform-response`, `stream-response`, `trigger-analytics`. A call refused by a plugin stops at the step of that plugin

start.description: When the step started, in milliseconds since the epoch

start_fmt.description: When the step started, as an ISO 8601 date

stop.description: When the step stopped, in milliseconds since the epoch

stop_fmt.description: When the step stopped, as an ISO 8601 date

duration.description: How long the step took, in milliseconds

duration_ns.description: How long the step took, in nanoseconds

ctx.description: What the step did. For `find-route`, the route that handled the call (`found_route`, its full json), the path it matched (`matched_path`) and the parameters of that path (`params`). For a step that runs plugins (`call-pre-route-plugins`, `call-access-validator-plugins`, `transform-request`, `transform-response`, ...), the sequence of those plugins: `plugins` lists each of them (`plugin`, its id, `name`, `duration`) with what it was given and what it answered (`execution_debug.in` and `execution_debug.out`, where `out.result.kind` is `successful` or `failure` for a transformer, `allowed`, `denied` (with the `status` of the refusal) or `failure` for an access validator)

ExecutionReport.description: The execution report of a call: every step the engine went through, with the plugins of each phase, what they were given, what they answered and how long they took

id.description: The id of the report, the snowflake of the request

creation.description: When the request reached the engine, as an ISO 8601 date

termination.description: When the engine was done with the call, as an ISO 8601 date

duration.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds

duration_ns.description: How long the call took, in nanoseconds

overhead.description: The time spent by otoroshi on the call, without the call to the backend, in milliseconds

overhead_ns.description: The time spent by otoroshi on the call, without the call to the backend, in nanoseconds

overhead_in.description: The time spent by otoroshi before the call to the backend, in milliseconds

overhead_in_ns.description: The time spent by otoroshi before the call to the backend, in nanoseconds

overhead_out.description: The time spent by otoroshi after the call to the backend, in milliseconds

overhead_out_ns.description: The time spent by otoroshi after the call to the backend, in nanoseconds

state.description: How the handling of the call ended

steps.description: The steps of the engine, in the order they ran

TryItResponse.description: The response of a trial, with the execution report of the call

status.description: The http status of the response the route answered. A call a plugin refused is answered with its status, the trial itself succeeds

headers.description: The headers of the response, the last value of each

body_base_64.description: The body of the response, encoded in base64

report.description: The execution report of the call. `null` when the route that handled the call, the one of the `find-route` step, is not one the admin behind the credentials can read, or when no route handled it

curl.description: A curl command that sends the same request
